title: Access & Procurement Fabric: Guidelines, Workflows, and Templates
author: Nina Kowalski
content:
Summary

This document defines the 'fabric' that ties together access and permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and the internal templates used to operationalize these processes. It is intended for request owners, approvers, people-ops, security, finance, and engineering managers.

Scope

- All employees, contractors, and third-party vendors requesting access to Redwood systems or requesting procurement/expenses.
- All changes to production services that require approvals or coordination with SRE, security, or product.
- Vendor lifecycle from intake to offboarding.

Principles

1. Least privilege first: grant the minimum rights required and require periodic recertification.
2. Single source of truth: all approvals and requests are recorded in the Ops Portal (internal).
3. Separation of duties: procurement approvals are separate from access approvals.
4. SLA-driven responsiveness: preset SLAs for different request types.

Owners & Escalation Paths

- Access & Permissions: Owner - People Ops (owner: Laura Chen). Escalation: People Ops Lead -> Security Manager (Greta Andersson) -> CFO on exceptions.
- Change Management: Owner - Eng Platform (owner: Mateo Rios). Escalation: Platform Lead -> Eng SRE -> CTO for high-risk rollouts.
- Procurement & Expenses: Owner - Finance (owner: Arjun Mehta). Escalation: Finance Manager -> Head of Finance -> CFO.
- Vendor Onboarding: Owner - Security & Legal joint (owner: Priya Nair).

SLAs and Targets

- Standard access request (non-privileged): target 3 business days.
- Privileged access (admin, production DB, infra): target 5 business days + security review.
- Procurement request (<= $5k): target 2 business days.
- Procurement request (>$5k): target 5 business days + legal/vendor review.

Access & Permissions Lifecycle

1. Request submission: submit via Ops Portal -> Select request type: Access - Application / Access - Infra / Temporary Privilege.
2. Tiered approval: Manager -> App Owner -> Security (if privileged) -> People Ops finalization.
3. Provisioning: automation kicks a runbook (where available) or IT team performs manual provisioning.
4. Recertification: automated reminders at 90/180 days depending on sensitivity; revocation if not recertified.
5. Emergency access: time-limited approval via 'just-in-time' (JIT) workflow; all sessions audited and recorded.

Access Request Example (Ops Portal JSON payload)

{
  "request_type": "access",
  "resource": "project-redwood-prod-db",
  "role_requested": "db_reader",
  "justification": "Support analytics job for Q4 cost report",
  "requested_by": "jordan.kim@redwood.com",
  "manager_approval": "pending"
}

Approval Matrix (Summary Table)

| Request Type | Approver Chain | Financial Threshold | Security Review Required | Typical SLA |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Non-privileged access | Manager -> App Owner | N/A | No | 3 business days |
| Privileged access | Manager -> App Owner -> Security -> People Ops | N/A | Yes | 5 business days |
| Purchase <= $5k | Manager -> Finance approver | $0 - $5,000 | No | 2 business days |
| Purchase > $5k | Manager -> Finance -> Legal (+Vendor Security if SaaS) | > $5,000 | Yes | 5 business days |
| Vendor onboarding | Vendor Lead -> Security -> Legal -> Finance | Varies | Yes | 10 business days |

Change Management (Engineering and Platform)

- All changes to production services must be registered in the Change Log (Ops Portal -> Changes).
- Change categories: Standard (pre-approved low risk), Normal (planned, requires change review), Emergency (unplanned, requires post-facto review).
- Change Review Board (CRB): weekly meeting for Normal changes that could impact availability or cost. CRB membership: Platform Lead, SRE, Security, Product Owner.

Change Request Checklist

1. Title and short description.
2. Risk assessment (low/medium/high).
3. Rollout plan and migration steps.
4. Backout plan and expected recovery time.
5. Monitoring & alerting hooks.
6. Stakeholder notifications (customers if needed).

Data Management & Classification

- Data classification levels: Public, Internal, Sensitive, Regulated.
- Handlers must label datasets and S3 buckets with classification tags and retention policies.
- Access to Sensitive/Regulated data requires additional approvals, data processing agreement (if external), and encryption at rest and transit.

Procurement & Expenses Workflow

1. Create procurement ticket in Ops Portal and attach vendor quote.
2. Include business justification and expected budget line (GL code).
3. Manager approval required for all purchases.
4. Finance performs spend validation and issues PO for approved vendors.
5. For SaaS vendors, require security & privacy questionnaire completion before PO if handling company data.

Procurement Approval Thresholds (Quick Reference)

- Up to $500: Manager discretionary; submit expense form and receipt.
- $501 - $5,000: Manager approval + Finance routing.
- $5,001 - $50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review.
- > $50,000: Exec sponsor + Finance + Legal + Procurement committee.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (minimum)

- Intake form completed with vendor contact and scope.
- Business justification and SOW or quote attached.
- Security questionnaire (SIG or vendor-specific) completed.
- Data processing agreement signed if vendor processes personal data.
- Procurement/PO issued and vendor entered into vendor registry.
- Key rotation and access expiry timeline agreed.

Vendor Offboarding

- Notify vendor of contract termination in accordance with contract terms.
- Revoke all credentials and API keys.
- Collect confirmation of data deletion or return per DPA.
- Update vendor registry and archive contract documents.

Travel & Expense Guidelines (high level)

- Preferred travel booking channels: company travel partner or expense portal.
- Per diem and meal caps referenced on the Expense Template.
- Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Higher-risk travel to regulated regions requires Security review and travel authorization form.

Templates (attached in the portal)

- Access Request Form (template ID: AR-2026): for employee and contractor access requests.
- Procurement Request Form (PR-2026): captures cost center, GL code, justification, vendor details.
- Vendor Intake Checklist (VI-2026): minimal fields for security and legal gating.
- Change Request Template (CR-2026): includes rollback plan and monitoring.
- Travel Authorization & Expense Template (TE-2026): per diem rates and receipt checklist.

Template Example (Procurement Request YAML)

requester: jordan.kim@redwood.com
department: Engineering
vendor: Acme Analytics
amount: 4200
gl_code: 5102
justification: Quarterly license for data pipeline profiling tool
required_by: 2026-02-01
approvers:
  - manager: rachel.turner@redwood.com
  - finance: arjun.mehta@redwood.com

Operational Playbook (step-by-step for a typical purchase)

1. Requester opens PR-2026, attaches quote and security questionnaire (if SaaS).
2. Manager approves in Ops Portal and selects GL code.
3. Finance reviews and either approves or requests clarifications.
4. If vendor handles data, Security triggers vendor review (up to 5 business days).
5. Legal drafts or reviews contract and DPA where necessary.
6. Finance issues PO and instructs Accounts Payable on payment terms.
7. Post-procurement: procurement record updated and vendor added to registry.

Audit & Reporting

- Quarterly audits on access recertification and high-value procurement (> $25k).
- Finance publishes a monthly spend dashboard by department and vendor.
- Security publishes a vendor risk dashboard showing outstanding questionnaires and remediation status.

Common Questions & Answers

Q: How do I get emergency access to production for a customer-critical fix?
A: Use the JIT workflow in Ops Portal and select Emergency access. The request will route to the on-call SRE and Security for immediate review; approvals can be retrospective but must include a full post-mortem within 3 business days.

Q: Who pays for consultant travel?
A: Consultant travel must be included in the SOW and pre-approved by Finance; expense claims must follow the standard expense template and manager review.
